questions.question: How fast does the body remove alcohol?

options.text: At a rate that changes based on how much alcohol is in the body.
At a constant rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body.
Faster if the person drinks coffee.
Faster if the person stays awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a constant rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up, like coffee or cold showers. The only way to become sober is to wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: A safe speed limit for cars may be unsafe for buses because:

options.text: It is usually safe for buses too.
It may be too fast for a bus.
It may be too slow for a bus.
It is the minimum speed buses should drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be too fast for a bus.
questions.explanation: Speed limits for cars may be unsafe for buses, especially on turns and curves. Large vehicle drivers must know the safe speed for their vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle has an inspection report, you should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find any issues yourself.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip your own inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. The repair company should have fixed any problems listed on it.

questions.question: When checking a cargo lift, make sure it:
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, and missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked in place.

questions.question: Brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting your brakes, check that the shoes and pads have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: When carrying multiple types of hazardous materials on a bus, the total weight must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Buses can carry no more than 500 total pounds of hazardous materials. Only 100 pounds of any single type is allowed.

questions.question: Windshield wiper blades should be:
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check wiper blades for damage and stiff rubber. Make sure they are secure and clean.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid, you do NOT need to:

options.text: Find where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, locate the power steering dipstick and check that there is enough fluid. The level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign that you are tired while driving?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble holding your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: If a trailer has ABS but the tractor does not, can you still use them together?

options.text: No, because both must have ABS.
Yes, but drive slower than normal.
No, you must find a tractor with ABS.
Yes, you can use them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you can use them together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on only the tractor or only the trailer still gives you better braking control.

questions.question: Where should carry-on bags be placed on a bus?

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where passengers can easily reach all emergency exits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where passengers can easily reach all emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Bags cannot be placed in doorways or aisles. All baggage must be secured so it does not damage, shift, or fall. It must not block the driver's movement or prevent passengers from exiting through any window or door in an emergency.

questions.question: Buses must never carry ____ in the passenger area.
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials where passengers are located.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment on a bus?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (if the vehicle does not have circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as reflective triangles.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails while driving?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after stopping completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it has slowed, brake gently and pull off the road. Then check your tires after coming to a complete stop.

questions.question: Which is a good rule when turning?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep your signal on during the entire turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Not brake because it could lock the wheels.
Hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not brake because it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking during a turn can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: During a trip, which item does NOT need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Check instruments, gauges, meters, and mirrors regularly during a trip. Also check tires, cargo, and lights for problems. The seat cushion does not need regular checking.

questions.question: What tool checks if tire pressure is correct?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure during the vehicle inspection test. Simply kicking the tires will not give a passing grade.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Use the taillights to alert other motorists.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Set out items from the cab to warn motorists.

questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. Place warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The correct amount of looseness varies by engine, so learn what is right for your vehicle.
